cards.lore: High mortality, severe disability. Proximal MCA or ICA occlusion.
cards.power: Total Shutdown. Contralateral hemiplegia, homonymous hemianopia, AND higher cortical dysfunction (dysphasia/neglect).

cards.lore: The most common stroke territory. Follows the motor homunculus.
cards.power: Dominant Disconnect. Contralateral hemiplegia + hemisensory loss. If dominant: Aphasia. Non-dominant: Neglect.

cards.lore: Hits medial frontal/parietal cortex. The filter is gone.
cards.power: Frontal Filter Failure. Contralateral leg weakness + sensory loss. Urinary incontinence + personality change (abulia).

cards.lore: Dizziness, Diplopia, Dysarthria, Dysphagia, Drop attacks. Highly dangerous to misdiagnose in the ED.
cards.power: Cross-Wiring. Produces crossed signs: ipsilateral cranial nerve palsy with contralateral long tract signs.

cards.lore: Caused by lipohyalinosis of deep perforators. Strongly linked to hypertension and diabetes.
cards.power: Pure Precision. Pure motor OR pure sensory stroke. NO cortical signs (no aphasia, neglect, or hemianopia).

cards.lore: PICA occlusion. Touch and proprioception are completely spared!
cards.power: Crossed Pain. Ipsilateral face pain/temp loss + contralateral body pain/temp loss. Ipsilateral ataxia and Horner's.

cards.lore: A devastating natural history. One of the few syndromes where thrombectomy is attempted well beyond 6 hours.
cards.power: The Lock-In. Quadriplegia, anarthria, but consciousness and vertical gaze are fully intact.

cards.lore: Macular vision is spared due to dual blood supply (MCA collaterals at the occipital pole).
cards.power: Alexia Without Agraphia. Contralateral homonymous hemianopia. Can write, but cannot read (if dominant).

cards.lore: Requires urgent dual antiplatelet therapy for high-risk patients. Do not ignore.
cards.power: The Warning Shot. Focal ischemia resolving within 24h (most <60m). High ABCD2 score mandates same-day review.

cards.lore: Ottawa SAH Rule: If CT is negative after 6h, mandatory LP for xanthochromia. Vasospasm risk days 4-14.
cards.power: Thunderclap. Worst headache of life, maximum severity at onset. Due to ruptured berry aneurysm.

cards.lore: IV alteplase eligible within 4.5 hours. Thrombectomy extends to 24h with favorable perfusion imaging.
cards.power: Salvage Operation. The target of all acute stroke therapy. Brain tissue that is ischemic but not yet dead.

cards.lore: Hypertensive small vessel (basal ganglia) vs. Amyloid angiopathy (lobar). Reverse anticoagulation instantly.
cards.power: Absolute Contraindication. Sudden focal deficit + headache, vomiting, reduced consciousness. NO tPA.

cards.lore: A dynamic, serial scoring tool. Essential for predicting the need for thrombectomy.
cards.power: Predictive Threshold. Score >= 6 suggests large vessel occlusion. Score < 4 is minor stroke.

cards.lore: ACcA is the most common site of berry aneurysms. Most humans have an incomplete circle, limiting collateral flow.
cards.power: The Redundancy Ring. Connects anterior/posterior circulations via communicating arteries (ACoA, PCoA).

cards.lore: Do NOT lower BP in acute ischemic stroke unless >220/120 or thrombolysis given.
cards.power: Time is Brain. Call EMS -> CT Head -> Ischemic & <4.5h = IV alteplase. If LVO = thrombectomy up to 24h.

cards.lore: High-intensity statin for ALL ischemic strokes regardless of baseline LDL. Carotid endarterectomy for symptomatic stenosis >50%.
cards.power: The Secondary Shield. Antiplatelet (non-cardioembolic) vs. Anticoagulant DOAC (cardioembolic AF).

cards.lore: Block D2 for psychosis, but you will worsen movement and raise prolactin simultaneously.
cards.power: The Quad-Core Modulator. Nigrostriatal (movement), Mesolimbic (reward), Mesocortical (motivation), Tuberoinfundibular (prolactin).

cards.lore: Loss of substantia nigra pars compacta. Hyposmia and REM sleep behavior disorder predate motor signs by YEARS.
cards.power: The Lewy Body Eraser. Resting tremor (4-6 Hz), lead-pipe rigidity, and mandatory bradykinesia.

cards.lore: Long-term use causes wearing-off, on-off fluctuations, and pulsatile-induced dyskinesias.
cards.power: The Trojan Precursor. Crosses BBB, decarboxylates to dopamine. Carbidopa stops peripheral conversion, saving the stomach.

cards.lore: Anticholinergic block: Mad as a hatter, dry as a bone, hot as a hare, red as a beet, blind as a bat.
cards.power: The Dual Empress. NMJ/autonomic transmitter (periphery) + memory transmitter from Nucleus basalis of Meynert (CNS).

cards.lore: Cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil) increase tone but do not halt progression. Anti-amyloids are the new frontier.
cards.power: The Slow Eraser. Episodic memory loss first -> language/visuospatial -> global decline.

cards.lore: Benzodiazepines increase opening frequency. Barbiturates increase duration (and can kill in overdose by acting as direct agonists).
cards.power: The Brain's Brake. Opens ligand-gated chloride channels to hyperpolarize the neuron.

cards.lore: In ischemia, massive glutamate release causes unchecked calcium influx and cell death (excitotoxicity).
cards.power: The Excitotoxic Accelerator. Fast excitatory transmission via NMDA/AMPA. NMDA requires coincidence detection.

cards.lore: Serotonin Syndrome = Mental status change + Autonomic instability + Neuromuscular clonus/hyperreflexia (differentiates from NMS rigidity).
cards.power: The Raphe Projector. Regulates mood, sleep, appetite. Blocked by SSRIs.

cards.lore: SNRIs (venlafaxine/duloxete) are highly effective for both depression AND neuropathic pain via descending pain pathways.
cards.power: The Sympathetic Driver. Arousal, attention, stress. SNRIs block both serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake.

cards.lore: First-generation antihistamines cross the BBB causing profound sedation. Second-generation do not.
cards.power: The Wakefulness Switch. H1 drives arousal in CNS. Loss of orexin activation causes narcolepsy.

cards.lore: Overdose triad = miosis, resp depression, reduced consciousness. Reverse with Naloxone (redose required for fentanyl).
cards.power: The Endogenous Suppressor. Mu receptor activation gives analgesia, euphoria, miosis, and respiratory depression.

cards.lore: A unique retrograde signaling mechanism. Epidiolex (CBD) approved for severe childhood epilepsies.
cards.power: The Backwards Messenger. Released postsynaptically, travels backwards to inhibit presynaptic neurotransmitter release via CB1.

cards.lore: Exogenous IV bolus briefly blocks AV node conduction—used therapeutically to terminate SVT.
cards.power: The Sleep Accumulator. Builds up during wakefulness to apply brakes. Caffeine is a non-selective antagonist.

cards.lore: The primary vascular vasodilator. Sildenafil blocks phosphodiesterase, potentiating this pathway. Toxic in stroke.
cards.power: The Receptorless Gas. Synthesized on demand. Diffuses freely across membranes to activate cGMP directly.

cards.lore: A single seizure is NOT epilepsy unless there is a high recurrence risk (e.g., epileptiform EEG or structural lesion).
cards.power: The ILAE Classifier. Focal (aware/impaired) vs. Generalized.

cards.lore: Driven by T-type calcium channels. Ethosuximide is first-line over valproate for girls (avoids teratogenicity).
cards.power: The Brief Interrupter. 5-30 second staring spells, dozens of times daily. Abrupt onset/offset, NO post-ictal confusion.

cards.lore: Always followed by post-ictal confusion/fatigue. Distinguish from syncope by prolonged post-ictal state.
cards.power: The Grand Mal. Tonic phase (sustained contraction, apnea) -> Clonic phase (rhythmic jerking).

cards.lore: 5-10m: IV Lorazepam. >20m: Levetiracetam/Valproate IV. Prolonged seizures internalize GABA receptors, becoming refractory.
cards.power: The Time-Critical Emergency. >5 min continuous, or 2+ seizures without recovery in between.

cards.lore: Severe neural tube defects. Absolutely avoid in women of childbearing potential unless NO alternative exists.
cards.power: The Broad-Spectrum Weapon. Blocks Nax, blocks T-type Ca2+, enhances GABA. Works for local, generalized, bipolar, migraine.

cards.lore: The preferred broad-spectrum agent in women of childbearing age. Counsel patients on mood disturbance/irritability.
cards.power: The Modern Workhorse. Binds SV2A modulating neurotransmitter release. Minimal drug interactions.

cards.lore: Valproate DOUBLES Lamotrigine levels. Carbamazepine halves them. Adjust dose carefully.
cards.power: The Slow Titrator. Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels. Must be titrated extremely slowly to avoid Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.

cards.lore: Devastating drug-drug interactions. Mandatory HLA-B*1502 screening for SJS risk in East Asian ancestry.
cards.power: The Auto-Inducer. First-line focal epilepsy and trigeminal neuralgia. Induces its own metabolism.

cards.lore: Give IV Ceftriaxone immediately. Do NOT delay antibiotics for CT or LP. Add dexamethasone for pneumococcal.
cards.power: The Ceftriaxone Race. Fever, neck stiffness, photophobia. Kernig's + Brudzinski's positive.

cards.lore: T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in temporal lobes. Start IV Aciclovir empirically BEFORE PCR results return. Delay is fatal.
cards.power: The Temporal Invader. Fever, headache, severe behavioral change, olfactory hallucinations.

cards.lore: Albuminocytological dissociation in CSF. Monitor FVC closely; intubate early. Steroids DO NOT WORK; use IVIg or Plasma Exchange.
cards.power: The Post-Infectious Climb. Acute immune polyneuropathy. Ascending areflexic weakness.

cards.lore: Myasthenic crisis = bulbar/respiratory failure. Differentiate from cholinergic crisis via Tensilon test. Treat with Pyridostigmine.
cards.power: The Fatigable Drop. Autoantibodies destroy postsynaptic nicotinic receptors. Fatigable weakness (worse with repetition).

cards.lore: Triptans (5-HT agonists) cause vasoconstriction—absolutely contraindicated in hemiplegic or brainstem aura migraines.
cards.power: Cortical Spreading Depression. Unilateral, throbbing, nausea, photophobia. 30% have aura.

cards.lore: NPH Triad: Gait apraxia, urinary incontinence, dementia. LP drainage test predicts shunt response.
cards.power: The Fluid Trap. Obstructive (aqueduct stenosis) vs. Communicating (impaired reabsorption).

cards.lore: Head 30 deg up, mannitol. Hyperventilation is strictly temporary (causes vasoconstriction to buy time). Steroids ONLY for tumor/abscess.
cards.power: Cushing's Reflex. Hypertension + bradycardia + irregular respiration = pre-herniation.

cards.lore: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure (CPP) = MAP - ICP. Hypotension starves the brain; hypertension worsens edema.
cards.power: The Secondary Preventer. Primary impact is done; your job is stopping secondary ischemia/hypoxia.

cards.lore: Uhthoff's phenomenon: Heat worsens symptoms due to conduction failure in already demyelinated axons.
cards.power: Dissemination in Time & Space. T-cell autoimmune demyelination. Optic neuritis, INO, Lhermitte's phenomenon.

cards.lore: Caudate nucleus degeneration disinhibits the motor pathway -> chorea, cognitive decline, psychiatric features.
cards.power: The Autosomal Expander. Trinucleotide repeat expansion. Anticipation: worsens in successive generations.

cards.lore: Co-existence of UMN and LMN signs in the same territory is the clinical hallmark. Riluzole extends survival modestly.
cards.power: The Dual Tract Destroyer. Attacks corticospinal tract AND anterior horn cells.

cards.lore: Nerve conduction distinguishes Demyelinating (slow velocity) vs. Axonal (reduced amplitude). Diabetes is the commonest cause.
cards.power: The Pattern Mapper. Length-dependent (stocking-glove), mononeuritis multiplex, or radiculopathy.

cards.lore: Compresses the crossing nasal fibers of the optic chiasm, causing loss of peripheral vision on both sides.
cards.power: The Chiasm Compressor. Most common pituitary tumor. Causes galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and visual field loss.

cards.lore: UMN (stroke) spares the forehead due to bilateral cortical innervation. Give prednisolone <72h. Tape the eye shut!
cards.power: The LMN VII Flattening. Unilateral LMN facial palsy. Affects the ENTIRE face, distinguishing it from an UMN stroke.

cards.lore: Caused by vascular compression of the nerve root. Carbamazepine is highly effective first-line.
cards.power: The Vascular Compressor. Lancinating, electric-shock pain in V2/V3 distribution triggered by light touch.

cards.lore: Untreated leads to blindness. Weight loss is the definitive treatment; Acetazolamide reduces CSF secretion.
cards.power: The Pseudotumor. Raised ICP without a mass. Daily headache, pulsatile tinnitus, visual obscurations.

cards.lore: Localize the lesion. Name the syndrome. Select the treatment. Map every decision. There is no hiding on the ward.
cards.power: Master Synthesis. A 70yo with aphasia/arm weakness. A 25yo with ascending areflexia. A 45yo with visual loss and headache.

cards.lore: The mechanics are real. The lore is real. Only the animals are fake. Draw your next patient. Stay fluffy!
cards.power: Draw Your Own. The ultimate Kayfabizzaro challenge.
